scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-MDMS.name: MDMS AMI read event log (system of record for AMI reads)

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

M-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-SHARE.name: Share of disputed bills built on ACTUAL meter reads

M-DISPUTE-RESPONSE-SLA-COMPLIA.name: Dispute ticket response time vs SLA

F-03.statement: Dispute ticket volume rose from 590 (2026-07) to 1180 (2026-08) and 1260 (2026-09), roughly doubling, after 610 (2026-06) (crm-tickets, E-02).

F-04.statement: Dispute ticket response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, across 2440 tickets (crm-tickets).

F-05.statement: No tariff change records were found in billing-db's tariff_change_log for the queried period.

F-06.statement: Manual-read route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts for period 2026-08..09 (route-log, E-05).

F-07.statement: Service contract §4.2 states the utility may request route priority changes, but they are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-08.statement: 320 accounts were estimated in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (billing-db, E-09).

F-09.statement: route-log identifies 14 distinct lagging routes with per-route completion values; sample shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion (E-10).

F-10.statement: Of disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 had an AMI read before cutoff that was exported to billing but rejected with billing_import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (mdms-export, E-12).

F-11.statement: Of disputed ESTIMATED bills, 56 had no AMI read received before cutoff and were not exported to billing (billing_import_status NO_READ_RECEIVED) (mdms-export, E-12).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: Dispute surge since August is caused by slow/manual ticket handling and lack of automatic bill correction; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors (e.g. in estimate substitution or read-type handling), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The nightly AMI read export from the vendor (H-MDMS-BILL) started failing or degrading around August, forcing more estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter read collection or the daily upload handoff from MeterWorks (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded around August, increasing missed/estimated reads and wrong bills.

H-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: Reduced field reading staffing/capacity caused incomplete routes and more estimated bills, as SH-FIELD's own account would frame it.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: Bills built on ACTUAL meter reads are themselves systematically erroneous (e.g. tariff misapplication or import rule issue), accounting for the majority of disputes (1785 of 3025, E-01), independent of estimate substitution.

H-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: Billing import validation rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution for valid reads and accounting for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-12).

interpretation_history.interpretation: Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type (billing-db, E-01), so the majority of disputes arise from bills built on actual (not estimated) meter reads. This weakens any causal story centered solely on estimate substitution and points toward errors also affecting actual-read billing, e.g. tariff or import-rule handling.

Monthly dispute counts (crm-tickets, E-02) show 610 in June, 590 in July, then a jump to 1180 in August and 1260 in September — confirming the initial claim that dispute volume roughly doubled starting in August. The data confirms timing and magnitude of the surge but says nothing about its cause.

Dispute ticket response times are well within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs a 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets, crm-tickets E-03), indicating slow/absent response handling is not driving the dispute surge. This directly weakens the initial-request framing (CL-01) and H-REQUESTER-FRAMING's premise that slow automated response is a cause the AI agent needs to fix.

The billing-db tariff change log returned zero records (E-04), meaning no tariff changes were logged in the queried period. This rules out a recent tariff change as the trigger for the dispute surge, narrowing H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR's "tariff misapplication" branch to a pre-existing application bug rather than a change-induced one, while the "import rule issue" branch and other hypotheses are untouched by this record.

Route completion for manual-read accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 accounts, during 2026-08..09 (route-log, E-05) — a real shortfall in field route completion during the dispute-surge window, but with no pre-August baseline given to show this is a change rather than a pre-existing gap.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this stakeholder statement corroborates the tool-authoritative E-04 finding (zero tariff_change_log records), reinforcing that a tariff change is not the trigger for the dispute surge. As a stakeholder claim it adds no new authoritative information beyond what E-04 already established.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims a shortfall of three meter readers since July has caused routes to run late, so affected customers get estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder account offering a specific mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already measured in E-05, but SH-FIELD has a stated incentive toward contract headcount increase, so it corroborates rather than independently proves the staffing cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The document confirms a contractual governance rule: any route priority change the utility requests of the field contractor must be confirmed at runtime by the Field Operations Manager before execution, consistent with the existing K-DISPATCH constraint on push_route_update. It speaks to authority/process for field dispatch actions, not to any cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db reports 320 accounts estimated in the last billing cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (account_id, route only; E-09). This gives the account-to-route mapping needed to join against route-log lagging-route data for the ESTIMATED-bill subset, but by itself does not yet show how much of the ESTIMATED subset is attributable to staffing/route delays.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log identifies 14 distinct routes as lagging, with per-route completion rates (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), providing the route-level detail needed to join against E-09's 320-account/40-route mapping to quantify the staffing shortfall's contribution to ESTIMATED-bill disputes (W-WI-STAFFING-SHARE-CHECK). It does not itself state what share of the 320 estimated-last-cycle accounts fall on these 14 lagging routes.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI reports MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), removing the access blocker that previously caused the mdms-export query for disputed-estimated AMI read events to fail with ACCESS_PENDING. This is a stakeholder claim about access status only; it does not itself establish whether the AMI/MDMS nightly export was actually degraded (U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH remains unanswered), and mdms-export tool health is still reported DEGRADED.

E-12 breaks the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (matching E-01's count) into two groups: 1184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read before cutoff that was successfully exported to billing yet rejected by billing import validation for high consumption (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), and only 56 (4.5%) had no read received at all. This shows the ESTIMATED-bill disputes are overwhelmingly caused by a billing import rejection rule discarding valid high-consumption AMI reads, not by AMI export failure or field staffing/route shortfalls, which can explain at most the small 56-record remainder.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.question: Does the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES via billing-config) actually show a change around August that explains the ACTUAL-read bill errors?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.decision_impact: If no rule change is found, H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE is falsified and the actual-read billing error cause must be re-investigated.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.resolution_path: Query billing-config tool for the rule change log in the Aug 2026 window and compare timestamps to the dispute surge onset.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.safe_placeholder: Do not implement or recommend any rule fix until the rule-change log is retrieved and reviewed; continue manual ticket handling in the interim.

U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.question: Is the Telemetrix AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or failing, contributing to the ESTIMATED-bill subset of disputes?
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.decision_impact: If AMI export is failing, estimate substitution for AMI-metered accounts needs vendor remediation distinct from the billing rule fix; mdms-export is currently DEGRADED with access ACCESS_PENDING (recovery_decision HOLD), blocking verification.
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.resolution_path: Vendor (ORG-AMI) must provision mdms-export access; then query read_events_for_disputed_estimated.
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.safe_placeholder: Treat H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE as open; do not rule in or out an AMI-side contribution to estimated-bill disputes.
U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.resolution: E-12 shows 1184/1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED bills had AMI reads received before cutoff and successfully exported_to_billing=true; export failure can explain at most the 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED cases, so the AMI/MDMS nightly export is not the primary driver of ESTIMATED-bill disputes.

U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.question: What share of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills is attributable to the field staffing/route-completion shortfall (E-05, E-07) versus other causes?
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.decision_impact: Determines whether a field-capacity recommendation to SH-FIELD is warranted alongside the billing-rule fix, or whether staffing is a secondary/pre-existing issue.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.resolution_path: Correlate route-log incomplete-route accounts with disputed ESTIMATED bills by account id.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.safe_placeholder: Keep field staffing framed as a contributing, not primary, hypothesis until the correlation is confirmed.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION-SHARE.resolution: E-12 shows 1184/1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED bills stem from billing import rejecting a valid pre-cutoff AMI read for high consumption, not from a missing/late field read; staffing-attributable missing-read cases are capped at 56/1240 (4.5%).

U-SUCCESS-MEASUREMENT-BASELINE.question: Is the pre-August monthly average (~600, from Jun-Jul) a valid baseline for G-1's 'back to baseline' target, or were Jun-Jul themselves already elevated?
U-SUCCESS-MEASUREMENT-BASELINE.decision_impact: Affects what dispute-volume threshold is used to judge resolution success.
U-SUCCESS-MEASUREMENT-BASELINE.resolution_path: Pull a longer historical window of monthly dispute volume pre-June if available.
U-SUCCESS-MEASUREMENT-BASELINE.safe_placeholder: Use the June/July average (~600) as a provisional baseline pending longer-horizon data.

A-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM.statement: The dispute surge is primarily driven by a change to billing import validation rules around August, inferred from the dominance of ACTUAL-read disputes (E-01) rather than confirmed via a direct billing-config rule-change-log query.

A-STAFFING-SECONDARY.statement: Field staffing shortfall and route-completion shortfall (E-05, E-07) are a secondary contributor affecting only the ESTIMATED-bill subset of disputes, not the primary driver of the overall surge.

A-TARIFF-RULED-OUT.statement: No tariff change this year (E-04, E-06) rules out tariff change as a trigger; this relies on the billing-db tariff_change_log being complete, though DA-BILL completeness is UNKNOWN.

A-SH-FIELD-INCENTIVE-BIAS.statement: SH-FIELD's staffing-shortfall account (E-07) may be inflated by an incentive toward contract headcount increase, though it is corroborated by the measured route-completion shortfall (E-05).

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

structural_remedies.description: Deterministically query the billing-config rule_change_log (DA-RULES) around the August window to confirm or falsify the suspected import validation rule change, closing VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a read-only query against an existing AUTHORITATIVE tool (billing-config) and requires no approval; it is a deterministic data step, not an agent task.; residual gap: Confirms but does not fix anything; if confirmed, the rule itself must still be reverted/corrected by Billing Ops and already-issued wrong bills still need correction.

structural_remedies.description: If the rule change is confirmed, Billing Operations (SH-BILL) reverts or corrects the specific import validation rule in billing-config under its own change-management process, outside the harness's read-only tool surface.
structural_remedies.rationale: K-BILLWRITE and the tool_surface show billing-config as read-only with no mutation path for the harness, so execution depends on an external human action by SH-BILL whose timing cannot be guaranteed within the remaining 225 minutes.; residual gap: Even once reverted, previously issued erroneous bills (1785 ACTUAL + part of 1240 ESTIMATED, E-01) remain uncorrected and dispute volume will not recover until re-billing occurs.

structural_remedies.description: Billing Operations manually reviews and issues corrected bills/credits for the ~3025 disputed accounts via human-approved write_bill_adjustment under K-BILLWRITE.
structural_remedies.rationale: K-BILLWRITE permits this only with SH-BILL approval and no automated writes; manually reviewing/adjusting thousands of bills exceeds the remaining 225-minute contest budget.; residual gap: Addresses the symptom backlog (SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-RECOVERY) but not the underlying rule error, and progress cannot be completed inside the contest window.

structural_remedies.description: ORG-FIELD restores the three missing meter readers (contract headcount) to close the route-completion gap (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-05) driving part of the ESTIMATED-bill disputes.
structural_remedies.rationale: Hiring/contract staffing changes are within SH-FIELD's contractual authority but inherently take longer than the remaining contest minutes to execute and show effect.; residual gap: Only addresses the secondary ESTIMATED-bill contributor (A-STAFFING-SECONDARY); leaves the dominant ACTUAL-read error driver (E-01) untouched, and SH-FIELD's account carries a disclosed incentive bias (A-SH-FIELD-INCENTIVE-BIAS).

structural_remedies.description: Resolve the vendor-provisioned MDMS export access needed to query AMI read events (DA-MDMS) and determine whether the nightly AMI export (H-MDMS-BILL) is degraded, closing VOB-U-AMI-EXPORT-HEALTH.
structural_remedies.rationale: The recovery_decision log shows a HOLD with stop_reason NOT_TRANSIENT and signature ACCESS_PENDING for mdms-export, meaning access is blocked by the external AMI vendor (ORG-AMI) and not resolvable by harness action within contest time.; residual gap: H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE and H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE remain unverified, leaving a HIGH-criticality unknown open before release regardless of other fixes.

proposal.summary: The problem (PD-1): billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (E-02), and Customer Service (SH-CS) initially framed this as a response-speed/automation gap requiring an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills (CL-01). Investigation established that response times are well within SLA (E-03) and no tariff change occurred (E-04, E-06), ruling out both of those as causes. The majority of disputed bills are built on ACTUAL meter reads, not estimates (E-01), and a deeper breakdown (E-12) shows 1184/1240 (95.5%) ESTIMATED-bill disputes involve a valid, successfully-exported AMI read that was nonetheless rejected by a billing import rule for high consumption, versus only 56/1240 (4.5%) with no read at all. This points to a billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, SUPPORTED) as the likely dominant driver, with field staffing/route-completion shortfall (E-05, E-07) only a minor, secondary contributor. The release decision is HOLD: the proposed package (ticket-pattern analysis plus a field route-capacity-review recommendation to SH-FIELD) failed Layer 1 verification because the capacity-review deliverable was only PARTIAL on completeness, and because E-12's evidence undercuts the staffing rationale behind that recommendation while the specific verification obligation asking for staffing-share quantification (VOB-R-3) is still OPEN and marked required before release.
